subject: ventures/sales-agent
professional: a sales-operations lead / SDR manager who runs cold outreach for a small B2B team, with a deliverability and email-compliance specialist checking the lead-magnet checkers

evidence.correctness: Ran 14+ probes through engine.triage(reply,'2026-11-08'), sendramp.plan and authcheck. Independent recomputation: (1) plan({mailboxes:3,targetPerDay:100}) gave 16 days, first-week total 285, schedule 30x3,45x3,60x3,75x3,90x3,100; a separate Python loop of the stated rule (start 10, +5 every 3 days, cap 40) gave the same 16 days, same sequence and 285. (2) plan({mailboxes:2,targetPerDay:50}) reached 50 on day 10; hand check 10+5*3=25 per box x2 = 50 on day 10, correct. (3) Dates checked against a Python calendar: 'until Monday 16 November' -> 2026-11-16 (a Monday), 'try me again in March 2027' -> 2027-03-01, 'after the 1st of February' -> 2027-02-01, German '1.12.2026' -> 2026-12-01, 'back in 2 wks' -> 2026-11-22 (14 days), '13/11/2026' -> 2026-11-13; all right. (4) SPF with 11 include: terms -> error 'allows at most 10' (RFC 7208 s4.6.4); DMARC pct=50 and p=banana flagged correctly. Wrong outputs found: "Please don't unsubscribe me, I love this!" and "Do not remove me from your list" both triage as unsubscribe (clear), i.e. negation is not handled, so a warm lead is suppressed with a fabricated consent record; '12/11/2026' and '3/4/2027' are read month-first (Dec 11, Mar 4) with no locale signal or warning, wrong by weeks for a European sender; 'Can you stop by next week?' -> interested (weak). Errors lean toward less contact, matching the stated design, but they are still wrong outputs. Ambiguity is not surfaced.
evidence.completeness: Checked claimed features by running them: inbox triage (10 categories) works; daily run, call prep, follow-up, research agent, pre-send checker, sequence checker, warm-up planner, list cleaner, auth checker, suppression reader all have modules and passing tests; self-host/ (IMAP poller, approval queue, SMTP, OAuth, CRM) has 25 passing tests. README and ROADMAP are candid that self-host, SMTP, OAuth, CRM write-back, --web, voice, M7 are tested only on fakes ('no real mailbox', 'no real CRM account'); M2 model scores and M5 are open, M5 blocked on the owner. I did not load the live page https://marisstella.app/sales-agent/ (no browser here), so 'Live tool' is unchecked, only page.test.mjs. Roughly: every feature works end to end on synthetic input, nothing on real mail, so 3 for 'done as described', capped by that disclosed gap.
evidence.verification: cd ventures/sales-agent && node --test '*.test.mjs': 219 tests, 219 pass, 1.4 s. self-host: 25/25 pass. Mutation 1 in core date logic (engine.mjs addBusinessDays weekend test 'w !== 0 && w !== 6' -> 'w !== 0'): 1 test failed ('dates: month-day, numeric, weekday, relative...'), caught. Mutation 2 (authcheck.mjs 'lookups > 10' -> '> 11'): 'SPF counts lookups and errors above 10' failed, caught. Both reverted with git checkout; git status clean. Weaknesses: many tests pin agent-written fixtures, the README admits the 'fresh' sets get spent once tuned on, and there is no test for negated unsubscribes, so the false-suppression defect passes everything. Real-data coverage exists only for 117+5 real bounce messages (tuned afterwards, README says so).
evidence.craft: Read sendramp.mjs, authcheck.mjs, parts of engine.mjs (729 lines), ROADMAP and README. Good: pure functions, no send path, explicit tests for that, input validation in plan(), a shared suppression reader after the duplicated-parser bug. Defects: engine.mjs is a single 729-line file of regex rule tables with dated 'added after N misses' patches (overfit-by-construction; the author's own ROADMAP says 100% tuned vs 37.5% fresh), no negation handling, locale-blind numeric dates, triage(reply, today) takes a YYYY-MM-DD string and throws 'Invalid time value' from iso() if given a number or Date (no argument validation, error is opaque; I hit it myself); authcheck estimates RSA bits from base64 length (ed25519 skipped) and SPF lookup counting does not expand includes (stated); the README is a ~120-line wall of dated changelog paragraphs.
evidence.claims: Claims checked against files: 'no send path, a test fails if one appears' (page.test.mjs, present, passes); '219 tests' style counts consistent with the run; bounce corpus 116/117 is labelled a tuned figure and NOTICE files exist for the Apache-2.0 and MIT corpora; fresh-set results (rules 27/41, 37.5%) are stated as low, not inflated; presend/authcheck/sendramp headers and pages say 'from memory, statute unread', 'rules of thumb, not provider limits', 'not legal advice'. This is unusually honest. Mild gaps: README says OOO dates read 'in 2 wks' etc. but does not state numeric dates are month-first; 'Why use this instead' compares against 11x/Artisan/Outreach without evidence about those products; the live-page claim was not loaded by me.
evidence.fitness: Job walked through: a founder pastes five replies, gets categories, a suppression CSV with the sentence as record, paused dates and approvable drafts; works. But the headline accuracy on text the rules had not seen is 37.5 to 66% (own eval/README), the model path (M2) is unmeasured, nothing was ever run on a real mailbox, CRM or call, and a user with the negation or dd/mm cases above would silently lose a lead or resume a week early. As an inbox sorter it is a useful assistant you must still review; as a trusted agent it is not yet reliable. The free checkers (pre-send, list, auth, ramp) are usable standalone.
evidence.domain: Compared against CAN-SPAM (physical address and opt-out are required on commercial email), CASL/PECR/UWG consent regimes, RFC 7208/7489/6376 and Google/Yahoo bulk-sender rules (spam complaints <0.3%, one-click unsubscribe). Method choices (stop on any ambiguity, suppress with the quoted sentence, drafts only, 10-lookup SPF limit, 2% bounce stop) are what a deliverability specialist would endorse. Departures: the compliance rules are admittedly written from memory of the statutes and 'primary sources unread', and a lawyer has not reviewed them; ramp defaults (10/day +5 every 3 days, cap 40) are folklore, not measured; SPF warns at 450 chars rather than the 255-per-string/512-byte constraint it cites; reply classification below a practitioner's trust threshold without the model path measured.

defects.what: Negated opt-out phrasing is classified as an unsubscribe: "Please don't unsubscribe me, I love this!" and "Do not remove me from your list" both return unsubscribe/clear, which suppresses the person and writes the sentence as a consent record.

All-numeric dates are parsed month-first with no locale signal or ambiguity warning ('back 12/11/2026' -> 2026-12-11, '3/4/2027' -> 2027-03-04); a European sender meaning 12 November would be paused about four weeks too long and the user is not told it was a guess.
Pre-send compliance rules per country are written from memory with statute texts unread and no lawyer review; the checkers say so, but a user may still rely on a 'clean' result.
triage() assumes today is a YYYY-MM-DD string; a number or Date throws an opaque 'Invalid time value' RangeError instead of a clear message.

Reply accuracy on unseen text is low (rules 27/41 and 37.5% on fresh sets per the project's own eval) and the hosted/local model scores (M2) are still unmeasured; no component has run on real mail, a real CRM or a real call.
SPF length warning uses 450 chars while the message cites 255 per string and 512 total; DKIM key size is inferred from base64 length and skipped for ed25519.

verdict: A large, unusually honest flagship (21 modules, 219 + 25 tests all passing, both seeded mutations caught, outputs I recomputed for the ramp planner, date reader and SPF/DMARC checker were right, and the claims are limited and sourced). It meets the computed bar narrowly (correctness, claims, verification all 3) but the craft, fitness and domain scores of 2 show the gap to a sales-ops or deliverability professional: reply sorting is regex rule tables that the project itself measures at 37.5 to 66% on unseen text, negation ('don't unsubscribe me') and dd/mm vs mm/dd are mishandled, compliance rules are from-memory, and nothing has touched a real mailbox, CRM or call. Finished as described (completeness 3) with the disclosed caveat that the integrations are tested only on fakes. Live page not loaded.
